rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: raw=[X-İd=1, x-id=2] walk: x-i̇d=[1];  expected:<[1, 2]> but was:<[1]>
rows.note: Lost value. X-\u0130d and x-id are one name by the rule (equalsIgnoreCase holds; req.header("x-id") answers 1), so HeaderEnumeration absorbs x-id into the first class, but the listed name is headerKey("X-\u0130d") = "x-i\u0307d" and headers("x-i\u0307d") does not match x-id (length differs, lowercases differ). Value 2 is reachable through no listed name. Root cause: DefaultRequest.HeaderEnumeration.matchesAny compares the new name with the first raw name, while headers(listedName) compares with its Locale.ROOT lowercase. The rule 'equalsIgnoreCase OR ROOT-lowercase equal' is not transitive around U+0130.

rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: raw=[x-id=1, X-İd=2, x-i̇d=3] walk: x-id=[1, 2]; x-i̇d=[2, 3];  expected:<[1, 2, 3]> but was:<[1, 2, 2, 3]>
rows.note: Double report. X-\u0130d matches x-id (equalsIgnoreCase) and x-i\u0307d (ROOT lowercase), but x-id and x-i\u0307d do not match each other. headerNames() lists both, and walking headerNames()/headers(name) reports value 2 twice, so a proxy forwarding from the enumeration would send that header line twice. Same non-transitivity root cause as LP-1.
